column3: The government's own master page: unclaimed property, back wages, tax refunds, pensions, bank failures, FHA refunds and more, all in one place.
Answer a few questions and it lists federal and state benefits you may be eligible for but aren't receiving.
The official NAUPA database searching most states at once. Start here, then confirm claims on each state's own site.

column2: Your state treasury's unclaimed property site
column3: Search every state you've lived or worked in — some aren't fully in MissingMoney. This directory links to all of them.
Check if the IRS is holding a refund for you, or if you left money behind by not filing a past return.
One of the most-missed credits — up to several thousand dollars for low-to-moderate income workers. Claimable for up to three prior years.
Refundable credit worth up to a few thousand dollars per child. Non-filers routinely miss it — you can still claim prior years by filing.
See balances, past payments, credits and any refund the IRS has on record for you.
Most state revenue departments have their own refund / unclaimed-refund lookup. Check every state where you filed.
A guided questionnaire across 1,000+ federal and state programs: income support, healthcare, housing, food, disaster aid and more.

column2: Medicare — Extra Help with drug costs
column3: If you're on Medicare, this and related cost-assistance can save thousands a year on prescriptions. Many eligible people never enroll.
The one form that unlocks Pell Grants, work-study and state aid. File it even if you think you won't qualify.
Grants for undergrads, teachers and specific fields that don't have to be repaid.
Public Service Loan Forgiveness, borrower defense, closed-school and disability discharge — and refunds of payments in some cases.
The government's guide to finding scholarships and grants. Never pay a service to 'find' scholarships — that's a scam.
Federal help paying heating and cooling bills, plus some crisis and weatherization aid. Run through your state or tribe.
Free home energy upgrades (insulation, sealing, repairs) that lower bills for income-eligible households.
A monthly discount on phone or broadband for eligible low-income households.
The USA.gov hub for utility and water assistance programs, including what replaced older water-bill aid.
ACA marketplace plans come with income-based premium tax credits that can cut your cost to very little. Check even if you've looked before.
Free or very low-cost health coverage for eligible adults and children. Eligibility is broader than most people think.
Check what you're eligible for — retirement, disability, and survivor benefits a family member's record may entitle you to.
Monthly payments for people with limited income who are 65+, blind or disabled. Separate from regular Social Security.
Monthly grocery benefits for eligible households. Millions who qualify don't apply.
Food, formula, and nutrition support for pregnant people and young children.
Help paying for child care so you can work or study. Run through your state.

column2: National Registry of Unclaimed Retirement Benefits
column3: Free search for retirement money left behind at former employers.
The federal agency that takes over failed pension plans holds unclaimed benefits for hundreds of thousands of people.
Find out who's now administering a retirement plan from an employer that disappeared.
For anyone who worked for the federal government: civil-service retirement and survivor benefits you may be owed.
Railroad workers and their families have a separate retirement and survivor system — benefits here aren't paid by Social Security.
Search by your name or a former employer to see if back wages are being held for you. Three-year window to claim.
Money left behind in federal court cases, including bankruptcies, held until the rightful owner claims it.
The consumer bureau's victim-relief fund repays people harmed by financial-company misconduct.
If you lost money to securities fraud the SEC prosecuted, a distribution fund may owe you.
Money owed to depositors and others from failed banks the FDIC closed.
The credit-union equivalent: deposits from liquidated federal credit unions.
Search for matured savings bonds and other Treasury securities tied to your name or Social Security number.
Regulators ask participating insurers to search their records for policies or annuities naming you as owner or beneficiary.
The VA holds unclaimed insurance payouts and dividends owed to veterans and their beneficiaries.
Check retired-pay accounts and records; former service members are sometimes owed money they never collected.
Disability compensation, pension, education, home loans and more — much of it unclaimed by those eligible.
The USA.gov hub explains who qualifies and links to HUD's lookup. Free — HUD never charges to issue a refund, so ignore any company that offers to get it for a fee.
Enter your ZIP to find rebates from utilities and manufacturers on appliances, HVAC and home upgrades you may already have bought.
Federal home-energy tax credits (insulation, heat pumps, solar, windows) that cut what you owe — many homeowners qualify and don't claim them.
Unused gift cards are real stored money. Most issuers have a free balance lookup — search the brand's name plus 'check balance' and use the card's own site.
Housing choice vouchers and subsidized housing that cap your rent at a share of income.
Grants (not just loans) for very-low-income rural homeowners, especially seniors, to repair and modernize a home.
One application for FEMA and other federal disaster help: housing, repairs, and other needs after a declared disaster.

Use the state directory, then separately search your county treasurer and municipal/clerk-of-court sites for 'unclaimed funds' or 'tax overage/surplus'. Free to claim — ignore 'surplus recovery' agents who want a cut.
A roundup of settlements currently accepting claims. Always file on the official administrator's site the listing links to, never a third party.
United Way's 211 connects you to local help: rent, utilities, food, emergency cash funds, and more, matched to your area. Free, 24/7 — dial 211 or search online.
Enter your ZIP to find free and reduced-cost programs near you — financial assistance, food, housing, health, and more.

Grants.gov lists federal grants, but be clear-eyed: almost all go to organizations, not individuals, and there is no general 'free government money for personal bills'. Anyone promising that is running a scam.
Banks pay $100–$400+ to open an account and meet simple terms. This tracker lists current, legitimate offers. Read the fine print (direct deposit, minimum balance, fees).
Companies pay $50–$200+ for an hour of feedback on products and apps. Sign-up is free; never pay to join a 'study'.
Similar paid-research marketplace, often higher-paying professional studies.
ClinicalTrials.gov and ResearchMatch list studies that often compensate participants. Compensation and risks vary — read the consent form.

column2: Cashback on shopping you'd do anyway
column3: Portals like Rakuten pay a percentage back on purchases you were already making. Modest, but real, and free to use.
If you're facing a real hardship, a well-told campaign shared with your network can raise meaningful money. Free to start; be honest and specific.
Dozens of cities run programs that send no-strings monthly cash to selected low-income residents. This tracks where they exist and who's eligible.
